solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Commercial centre with mail having special delivery

indicators.note: a special delivery hands these letters over in a fresh, unusual order

explanation.surface: A commercial depot where mail is handled by special delivery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'special delivery' reads as a postal service but signals rearranging CENTRE and MAIL together.
explanation.definitionFit: Mercantile is a synonym of commercial, describing trade and merchants.

clue.text: Girl upsetting her best friend, not half!

indicators.note: in a down clue upsetting turns the remaining letters upside down, so they read backwards
not half says half of the word is dropped, leaving its first four letters

parts.note: the saying goes that diamonds are a girl's best friend

explanation.surface: A girl falling out badly with her best friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not half' cuts DIAMONDS to DIAM, and 'upsetting' turns DIAM over to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A maid is an old-fashioned word for a young woman or girl.

clue.text: Adopts a different position as elector suffering

indicators.note: suffering suggests the letters are knocked about and rearranged

explanation.surface: An unhappy voter moves elsewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suffering' rearranges the letters of AS ELECTOR.
explanation.definitionFit: To relocate is to move to a new place, so it means taking up a different position.

clue.text: There's place for sacrifice — change is being mentioned

indicators.note: being mentioned says a word is spoken, so we want one that sounds the same

parts.note: to change something is to alter it

explanation.surface: A remark that change is under discussion at the place of sacrifice.
explanation.definitionFit: Altars are the raised tables where offerings and sacrifices were made in temples.

clue.text: English bishop involved in row is an eager person

indicators.note: involved in places the English bishop inside the row

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats
RR stands for Right Reverend, the title of a bishop

explanation.surface: An English bishop caught up in a quarrel is keen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' looks like a quarrel but means a line of seats. RR stands for Right Reverend, the title used for a bishop.
explanation.definitionFit: Terrier can mean a tenacious, keen person, from the eagerness of the dog breed.

clue.text: Old doctor entertained by fat Italian citizen

indicators.note: entertained by puts the old doctor inside the fat, like a guest

parts.note: lard is pig fat
MB is a Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: An old doctor is wined and dined by a fat Italian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fat' looks like a description of the Italian, but it is the noun LARD.
explanation.definitionFit: A Lombard is a native of Lombardy, the region of northern Italy around Milan.

clue.text: Injury in thigh restricting run

indicators.note: restricting has the thigh hemming in the run, so one goes round the other

parts.note: the ham is the back of the thigh
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A thigh injury that stops someone running.
explanation.definitionFit: Harm means damage or hurt done to someone, an injury.

clue.text: Mountains within American desert

indicators.note: within says the answer sits inside the clue words that follow

explanation.surface: Mountains rising in an American desert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'within' points to the letters inside AMERICAN DESERT.
explanation.definitionFit: The Andes are the long mountain range down the west of South America.

clue.text: Something in steel that makes main street look awful

indicators.note: making something look awful jumbles it, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A steel component that spoils the look of a high street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'look awful' rearranges the letters of MAIN STREET.
explanation.definitionFit: Martensite is the hard crystal structure that forms in quenched steel, its main constituent when hardened.

clue.text: One place seen when looking across lake?

definitions.text: One place seen when looking across lake?

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: something looking across another spans it, so the place goes round the lake

parts.note: to set something is to place it
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A spot you might notice when gazing out over a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: a small island is just what you see across a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: An islet is a small island, the kind of spot seen out on a lake.

clue.text: Cue bridging a rest

indicators.note: bridging means the cue stretches across the A, holding it inside

parts.note: a cue is a prompt or reminder

explanation.surface: A snooker cue laid across a rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cue' and 'rest' suggest snooker, but a cue here is a prompt.
explanation.definitionFit: The remainder is what is left over, the rest.

clue.text: Wild animals naughty child sits on unfortunately

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sitting on another is placed above it

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child
alas is an exclamation meaning unfortunately

explanation.surface: A naughty child sits on wild animals, sadly.
explanation.definitionFit: Impalas are African antelopes, wild grazing animals.

clue.text: Is legendary bird seen around about a Mediterranean island

indicators.note: seen around means the words before it are turned round to read backwards

parts.note: the roc is a giant bird of Arabian legend
C is short for circa, about

explanation.surface: A mythical bird spotted circling a Mediterranean island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen around' turns the first two pieces together as one run, not just the bird; 'around' tempts a container reading, but nothing fits inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Corsica is a French island in the Mediterranean, north of Sardinia.

clue.text: That's not proper ice stick

definitions.meaning: ice is slang for diamonds, and ... is the glassy stuff of fake gems

explanation.walkthrough: Ice is slang for diamonds, so fake jewellery is 'not proper ice'.
explanation.definitionFit: Paste is both imitation-gem glass and an adhesive used to glue things.

clue.text: Part of what coin counterfeiter must do to speed up successfully?

definitions.text: Part of what coin counterfeiter must do
definitions.meaning: a faker of coins has to fake the monarch's portrait on one side

explanation.walkthrough: Split it 5,1,4: a counterfeiter must forge a head on the coin.
explanation.definitionFit: To forge ahead is an idiom for making strong progress, moving forward fast.

clue.text: Revolutionary time has to be right, with commander leading

indicators.note: leading puts the commander at the front of the rest

parts.note: OC stands for Officer Commanding
taken as written

explanation.surface: A revolution's timing must be correct, with a commander in front.
explanation.walkthrough: Russia's October Revolution of 1917 makes the month a 'revolutionary time'.
explanation.definitionFit: The October Revolution brought the Bolsheviks to power, so the month is a time of revolution.

clue.text: Something absorbing in the writer's study?

definitions.text: Something absorbing in the writer's study?

parts.words: Something absorbing in the writer's study
parts.note: absorbing reads as fascinating, but means soaking up ink on a writer's desk

explanation.walkthrough: 'absorbing' suggests a gripping book; the real sense is soaking up ink.
explanation.definitionFit: Blotting paper on a desk soaks up wet ink, an absorbent sheet.

clue.text: To accommodate dead, the underworld widens out

indicators.note: to accommodate is to take in, so the underworld holds the dead

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld and his realm
late means dead, as in the late king

explanation.surface: The underworld expands to make room for the dead.
explanation.walkthrough: Dis is the Roman underworld.
explanation.definitionFit: Dilates means expands or widens, as pupils do in the dark.

clue.text: For me level tar may be spread on top of road

definitions.text: For me level tar may be spread on top of road

indicators.note: spreading the letters out jumbles them into a new order
on top of picks the first letter of road, its top in a down clue

explanation.surface: Someone on the move welcomes smooth tar laid on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines: a traveller benefits from a newly surfaced road.
explanation.definitionFit: A traveller is someone on a journey, who uses the roads being surfaced.

clue.text: Two games in Hants town

parts.note: Go is a Japanese board game
sport is any game played competitively

explanation.surface: A Hampshire town that offers a pair of games.
explanation.walkthrough: Hants is the abbreviation for Hampshire, a county on England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Gosport is a naval town in Hampshire, opposite Portsmouth.

clue.text: Coach is means of transport taken with hesitation

parts.note: a train is a means of transport
er is the sound of hesitating

explanation.surface: A coach is a mode of travel taken hesitantly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coach' looks like a bus, beside 'means of transport', but means a sports instructor.
explanation.definitionFit: A trainer coaches athletes, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Sung part 'notedly superior'?

parts.note: a vocal line that sits above the main tune, superior in pitch

explanation.walkthrough: 'superior' means pitched higher, not better.
explanation.definitionFit: A descant is a decorative melody sung above the main tune of a hymn.

clue.text: I have risen in party — American playing dirty

indicators.note: in puts the turned letters inside the party

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: in a down clue risen means the letters go upwards, read backwards

parts.note: I've is short for I have

explanation.surface: A rising party member plays dirty with an American.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'risen' means read upwards. 'playing dirty' is an adjectival phrase here, like underhand.
explanation.definitionFit: Devious means underhand or scheming, the attitude of someone playing dirty.

clue.text: A mostly boring time makes you blue?

indicators.note: mostly means all but the final letter is kept

parts.note: dull means boring

explanation.surface: A boring stretch of time leaves you feeling sad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blue' looks like sad, but means risqué.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue jokes or films are sexually explicit, the same sense as adult content.

clue.text: Superior meal but without starter

indicators.note: without starter takes away the first letter of the word

parts.note: supper is an evening meal

explanation.surface: A fine meal, though missing a first course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starter' looks like a first course, but means the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Upper means higher in rank, a synonym of superior.

clue.text: Unfavourable bit from chapter of the NT, say?

parts.note: the New Testament events are dated AD, anno Domini
a verse is a numbered part of a Bible chapter

explanation.surface: An unwelcome passage from a New Testament chapter.
explanation.walkthrough: AD, anno Domini, labels the years after Christ, the period of the New Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: Adverse means hostile or harmful, the opposite of favourable.

clue.text: This person in love repeatedly kept under by right lover

indicators.note: in a down clue being kept under puts the rest below the right
in places this person inside the pair of loves
repeatedly says the letter for love is used twice

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, written as O
me is the setter speaking about this person

explanation.surface: Someone hopelessly in love, kept down by a proper lover.
explanation.walkthrough: Romeo is Shakespeare's young lover, and a byword for one.
explanation.definitionFit: A Romeo is a passionate male lover, after Shakespeare's hero.

clue.text: A negative word being spoken is a difficulty

indicators.note: being spoken says the word is said out loud and sounds like another

parts.note: not is the word of negation

explanation.surface: Saying no causes a problem.
explanation.definitionFit: A knot is a tangle, so figuratively a difficulty or problem.

clue.text: Person at end of line misconstrued language

indicators.note: end of picks the last letter of line
misconstrued suggests the words are misread, taken in a jumbled order

explanation.surface: Someone at the end of the queue misunderstood the language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misconstrued' rearranges PERSON, AT and E, the last letter of 'line'.
explanation.definitionFit: Esperanto is an artificial language created in the 1880s for international use.

clue.text: Motorway lane cut short in city

parts.note: M1 is the London-to-Leeds motorway, written MI in crosswords

indicators.note: cut short removes the final letter of the word

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A motorway lane is shortened near a city.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, its 1 read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Milan is the major city of northern Italy, capital of Lombardy.

clue.text: Dreadful day I recall with no phone

indicators.note: with no says the following piece is taken away from the word

parts.note: taken as written
to call is to phone

explanation.surface: A dreadful day remembered without a telephone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'phone' is CALL, taken out of RECALL to leave RE.
explanation.definitionFit: Dire means terrible, so it is a synonym of dreadful.

clue.text: Fantastic actor, I star as one of the landed gentry maybe

definitions.text: one of the landed gentry maybe

indicators.note: fantastic suggests something wild and fanciful, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A brilliant actor claims to star as a member of the gentry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fantastic' rearranges ACTOR, I and STAR.
explanation.definitionFit: An aristocrat is a noble, and the landed gentry are an example of the upper class.
